newsitem.title: FRANCE: Nostalgia as ex-France liner docks in former home.
newsitem.headline: Nostalgia as ex-France liner docks in former home.

text.p: Thousands thronged this French port in an outburst of patriotic nostalgia on Tuesday as the liner Norway, originally named France, docked at its home port for the first time in 17 years.

The majestic 315-metre-long (1,040 ft) blue ocean liner, once the symbol of French style and luxury, called at Le Havre on the north coast on a cruise from New York before heading to Britain for repairs.
Then the world's largest liner, the France was launched in 1960 for France's Compagnie Generale Transatlantique (CGT) to carry passengers on prestige crossings between Le Havre and New York.

Hurt by the rapid development of jetliners and oil price hikes, the CGT turned to luxury Caribbean and South American cruises but had to decommission the France in 1974 when the government refused to keep footing the bill for losses.

The liner was bought in 1979 by the Norwegian Cruise Line, fitted with smaller engines and refurbished at Bremerhaven in Germany to increase the number of berths. Re-named Norway, it is now used for Caribbean cruises.
